{{Quote|Hey, ''I'' want ''in'' on this action!|translated=1|Weazel|<ref name="Podracing Tales">"[[Podracing Tales]]"</ref>}}
'''Weazel''' was a diminutive [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Arms dealer/Legends|weapons dealer]] who lived and worked on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. In that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], he attended the [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing/Legends|Podrace]] on Tatooine and sat in the viewing box of his acquaintance, the [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] [[Watto/Legends|Watto]], in the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena/Legends|Mos Espa Grand Arena]]. During the race, he [[Gambling/Legends|gambled]] on the result with Watto and the [[Anx/Legends|Anx]] [[Graxol Kelvyyn/Legends|Graxol Kelvyyn]], wagering twenty [[Wupiupi/Legends|wupiupi]] that the [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|Podracer]] of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]&mdash;a [[Youngling/Legends|young]] [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] to Watto&mdash;would cross the finish line. Good fortune came his way when Skywalker ultimately won the race. Later that year, Weazel and a [[Unidentified Trandoshan arms dealer|Trandoshan associate]] of his were selling [[Weapon/Legends|arms]] at the Tatooine trading site known as [[Mochot Steep/Legends|Mochot Steep]] when it was [[Attack on Mochot Steep|attacked]] by a band of [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|You're really betting against your own slave, Watto?''&raquo;<br />&laquo;''Indeed I am, Weazel! My money's on Sebulba!|translated=1|Weazel and Watto, at the Boonta Eve Classic|<ref name="Podracing Tales" />}}
[[File:WeazelE1.jpg|thumb|right|225px|Weazel watched the Boonta Eve Podrace from Watto's box.]]
The stocky<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|323|Weazel}}</ref> [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="Outlander" /> Weazel lived on<ref name="CSWE" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] leading up to<ref name="CSWE" /> [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> He<ref name="Outlander" /> worked as a [[Arms dealer/Legends|weapons dealer]] on the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] planet and had several acquaintances, including a [[Unidentified Trandoshan arms dealer|Trandoshan]] with whom he sometimes dealt [[Weapon/Legends|arms]] and the [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] [[Watto/Legends|Watto]].<ref name="CSWE" /> In 32 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> Weazel attended the [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing/Legends|Podrace]] near the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] at the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena/Legends|Mos Espa Grand Arena]], and, along with several of Watto's other associates, joined the Toydarian in his [[Watto's box/Legends|private viewing box]] to watch the race. One of Watto's [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] workers, a [[Youngling/Legends|young]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] named [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], was entered in the event, and when the boy's [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|Podracer]] failed to start at the commencement of the race, Weazel and the other occupants of Watto's box laughed and jeered.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />

Skywalker quickly overcame his [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer's]] difficulties,<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> and as he raced to catch up to his opponents, Weazel, Watto, and the [[Anx/Legends|Anx]] [[Graxol Kelvyyn/Legends|Graxol Kelvyyn]] began to [[Gambling/Legends|place bets]] on whether or not his vehicle, cobbled together from spare parts, would complete the race. Although Watto gambled against his own slave, Weazel and Kelvyyn both wagered twenty [[Wupiupi/Legends|wupiupi]] that Skywalker would cross the finish line. After the [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|racer]] [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]] completed the first of three laps in record [[Time/Legends|time]], Watto and Kelvyyn bet on whether he would set a record for the entire race, but Weazel balked at the asking price of fifteen wupiupi and sat out of the gamble.<ref name="Podracing Tales" /> Skywalker eventually overtook Sebulba and won the race, and although Watto argued with his comrades,<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> Weazel and Kelvyyn insisted that he pay them the money he owed.<ref name="Podracing Tales" />

[[File:Weazelmakingmoney.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Weazel and his Trandoshan associate sell arms at Mochot Steep.]]
Later in the year, Tatooine's indigenous [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] grew increasingly violent and raided several settlements under the leadership of [[Sharad Hett]], a former [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]&ndash;turned&ndash;Tusken [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]]. After a particularly brutal [[Raid on Anchorhead|attack]] on the city of [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]], residents of the surrounding area began to purchase large quantities of weapons. Weazel and his [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] acquaintance set up shop at the trading site known as [[Mochot Steep/Legends|Mochot Steep]] and sold arms that were being [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggled]] past official checkpoints by others. Three [[Standard day/Legends|days]] after the attack on Anchorhead, they were at Mochot Steep when Hett's Tuskens arrived. The raiders announced their presence by shooting and [[Death/Legends|killing]] the Trandoshan, and the trading site's denizens frantically attempted to evacuate during the subsequent [[Attack on Mochot Steep|slaughter]].<ref name="Outlander" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Tough luck, Watto! Pay up!|translated=1|Weazel, smugly demanding payment after a bet|<ref name="Podracing Tales" />}}
[[File:Weazelattheraces.png|thumb|right|250px|Weazel laughs at Anakin Skywalker's plight during the Boonta Eve Classic.]]
Standing at less than 1.37 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall,<ref name="Height" /> Weazel was considered short and stocky for his [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="CSWE" /> Possessing [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and light skin, he wore his brown [[Hair/Legends|hair]] down to his shoulders.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> He was considered by others to be sleazy.<ref name="Menace Revisited">{{InsiderCite|109|Menace Revisited}}</ref> Although he was highly amused when Anakin Skywalker's Podracer would not start,<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> Weazel was critical of Watto for betting against his own slave and won twenty wupiupi from the Toydarian for wagering that Skywalker would finish the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve race]]. He was eager to gamble against Watto and was smug in his victory when the time came for Watto to pay him.<ref name="Podracing Tales" />

==Skills and abilities==
Weazel was fluent in [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]].<ref name="Podracing Tales" />

==Equipment==
At Watto's box<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> and at Mochot Steep,<ref name="Outlander" /> Weazel wore brown [[Robe/Legends|robes]] over a tan shirt, with pants matching the shirt color, and brown [[Boot/Legends|boots]].<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Origins, ''Phantom Menace'', character name===
{{Quote|The character I was set to play was originally a masked character, and I think that once George had written it and wanted me to play it, he sort of had second thoughts about putting me inside a mask again. So he came up with this idea of putting me in the Podrace watching in Watto's box. They glued these extensions in my hair, and everyone mistook it for Willow watching the Podrace.|Warwick Davis|<ref name="Davis CIII">{{SWArchive|url=community/event/celebration/f20050419/indexp30.html|text=starwars.com at Celebration III - Your Host: Warwick Davis}} {{C|Additional [https://web.archive.org/web/20060104005003/http://www.starwars.com/community/event/celebration/f20050419/indexp30.html backup link]}}</ref>}}
Weazel first appeared in<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> the [[May 19]], [[1999]]<ref name="TPM date">{{SW|url=news/phantom-menace-memories|text=Our Favorite Memories of the Release of ''Star Wars: The Phantom Menace''}}</ref> [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], in which he was portrayed by veteran ''[[Star Wars]]'' actor [[Warwick Davis]]. Davis was famous for playing [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket]] the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] in [[1983]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']],<ref name="Davis CIII" /> and in ''The Phantom Menace'', he was called on to play four roles: Weazel; the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] child [[W. Wald|Wald]]; the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] in several of Yoda's walking scenes; and an [[Grimey|extra]] seen roaming the streets of Mos Espa.<ref name="Valley">{{InsiderCite|67|Beyond the Valley of the Ewoks}}</ref> Davis was initially hired to only play Wald, a masked character, but director [[George Lucas]] decided during filming that he wanted Davis to appear onscreen unmasked. He accordingly placed Davis inside Watto's viewing box during the Podrace scene, and after [[Wikipedia:Artificial hair integrations|hair extensions]] were glued onto Davis's head, the character of Weazel was born.<ref name="Davis CIII" />

Davis's scene was filmed over one day at [[Leavesden Studios]] in [[Wikipedia:England|England]], where, in his own words, he was "basically sitting in bleachers and moving my head left to right." With that information published in the [[August]]/[[September]] [[1998]] "[[When Artoo Met Wicket]]" article in [[Star Wars Insider 39|''Star Wars Insider'' 39]], that source was Weazel's first inclusion in official ''Star Wars'' media, predating ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="When Artoo met Wicket">{{InsiderCite|39|When Artoo Met Wicket}}</ref> The actors in the box were subject to blowing fans that represented the Podracers' exhaust. The scene was filmed from various angles, and during the shoot, indigestion from the on-set snacks and bright lights that simulated Tatooine's twin [[Star/Legends|suns]] combined to cause Davis to fall asleep until Lucas woke him up.<ref name="Insider 143">{{InsiderCite|143|Warwick Davis Presents: A Star Wars Acting Master Class|Warwick Davis Presents: A ''Star Wars'' Acting Master Class}}</ref>

Weazel also appeared, and was first identified by name, in the [[Star Wars (1998) 7|seventh issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars: Republic]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series,<ref name="Outlander" /> released on [[June 23]], 1999.<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/53902/star_wars_1998_7|text=Star Wars (1998) #7}}</ref> Watto's viewing box does appear in the film's [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|video game]] adaptation, though Weazel is absent as the box is populated only by Watto, Graxol Kelvyyn, a [[Droid/Legends|droid]], and a [[Watto's flunky|flunky of Watto's]].<ref name="Video Game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref>

===April Fool's 2006===
[[File:Willow.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Warwick Davis as Willow Ufgood in 1988's ''Willow'']]
As Weazel, Wicket, Wald, and [[Thorn Drumheller|Willow Ufgood]]&mdash;a magic-using character that Davis played in [[Lucasfilm]]'s [[1988]] [[Wikipedia:Sword and sorcery|sword-and-sorcery]] film [[Willow (film)|''Willow'']]&mdash;all begin with the letter W, Davis has joked that he created a long list of W names and gave it to Lucas to consult whenever he was called upon to play a new character.<ref name="Return to Endor">{{InsiderCite|62|Return to Endor: The Stars of the Ewok Films Remember Their Adventure}}</ref> According to Davis, when fans saw the Podracing scene, many of them mistook Weazel for Ufgood, who was similarly long-haired when played by Davis.<ref name="Davis CIII" /> Seven years after the release of ''The Phantom Menace'', the two characters were equated as part of an [[Wikipedia:April Fools' Day|April Fool's Day]] joke that featured a mock-serious [https://web.archive.org/web/20080325023230/www.starwars.com/databank/updates/401/news20060401.html update] to the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] on [[April 1]], [[2006]]. Entries on several characters and locations from ''Willow'' and its sequel novels, the [[Wikipedia:Willow (1988 film)#Novels|''The Shadow War Chronicles'']], were added to the Databank, which stated that the series was now a part of ''Star Wars'' [[canon]] and that its events took place on [[Andowyne]], a remote world located deep in the [[Kathol Rift/Legends|Kathol Rift]].<ref name="Joke">{{SWArchive|url=databank/updates/401/news20060401.html|text=The Shadow War Chronicles}}</ref>

The [https://web.archive.org/web/20080315035854/http://www.starwars.com/databank/updates/401/character/thorndrumheller Databank entry] on Ufgood, a.k.a. Thorn Drumheller, claimed that he experienced strange otherworldly [[Dream/Legends|dreams]] between the events of ''Willow'' and ''The Shadow War Chronicles'', one of which brought him to Tatooine, "a world entirely wrapped in harsh deserts, and populated with many bizarre and wondrous beings." Ufgood took the alias of "Weazel" and used his [[Magic/Legends|magical]] abilities to impress Watto, who invited him into his private viewing box at the Mos Espa Grand Arena in the hope that Ufgood's magical abilities would bring him good luck in his gambling endeavors. Ufgood later woke up on Andowyne with a sunburn and a parched throat as the only evidence of his bizarre trip to another world.<ref name="Thorn">{{DB|updates|401/character/thorndrumheller|Drumheller, Thorn}} {{C|[https://web.archive.org/web/20080409103631/www.starwars.com/databank/updates/401/character/thorndrumheller backup link] on [[Wikipedia:Internet Archive|Archive.org]]}}</ref>
